Theme

Latin word

sententia

sententia, sententiae f.

noun, first declension

a judgment, the view one has come to; opinion, view, judgement; a motion (in a meeting); a view put forward; a sentence; a senator’s vote: the opinion he states when asked

In this lexicon

  • decision

    also used · classical · Plaut. Pers. 373: ego dē hāc sententiā nōn dēmovēbor

  • opinion

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. Ph. 454: quot hominēs, tot sententiae; Cic. Att. 7.13a.3: vir meā sententiā magnus; Traupman 21, 354

  • propose

    also used · classical · Traupman 178: Quis in Crassī sententiam īvit?, Who supported Crassus’ proposal?

  • sentence

    the recommended word · classical · Hor. S. 1.10.9: ut currat sententia; Quint. 9.3.45: initia et clausulae sententiārum (Lewis & Short); Traupman 27, 34, 248

  • vote

    also used · classical · Traupman 181: discessiō facta est in ejus sententiam, a vote was taken on his motion

    great things are done not by strength or speed or quickness of body, but by planning, authority and judgmentCic. Sen. 17
